children: Hopes of China committing to buy more Boeing
planes are fading ahead of the summit between Donald Trump and Xi Jinping on Thursday,
Reuters
reported, citing two people briefed on the matter.
Boeing
is instead working to finalize a provisional deal for China to buy 200 planes, which was struck in tandem with Trump's summit with ​Xi in May.
The aircraft maker has been effectively shut out of China since 2017, while its rival Airbus
continued to expand its market share in the country.
According to Boeing
and Airbus
forecasts, China is expected to ⁠order around 9,000 new planes by 2045 – more than any other region.
Boeing

and China had been discussing a potential deal for 500 planes ahead of the Trump-Xi summit in May, before provisionally agreeing on a 200-jet order. At the time, Trump said China could boost its ‌⁠order to as many as 750 planes.
Last week, Boeing
CEO Kelly Ortberg said the important part was to reopen the China market for the company. "I think there will be an
going forward," he said. "They're going to be announced by the airlines at their pace, however they want to announce those."
Securing new aircraft deals was not a top priority at Thursday's summit, Scott Kennedy, a China specialist at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, told
Reuters
U.S. and Chinese officials are more focused on the countries' trade truce, AI safeguards, weapons sales to Taiwan, and deals on soybean and rare earth exports, Kennedy added.
